setting: You're in the spice aisle of a grocery store on a Saturday afternoon. Two adult women are shopping together. Jasmine, the one holding a jar of smoked paprika, makes eye contact and smiles. Her friend Renee is reading a recipe on her phone. Say whatever you'd naturally say.

characters.name: Renee
characters.trait: dry humor, a bit guarded at first

open_good.speaker: jasmine
open_good.text: Ha, hi! Okay, honest opinion: smoked paprika or regular? We're making chili tonight.

open_good.speaker: renee
open_good.text: She's been holding that jar for five minutes. Help us.

context.speaker: jasmine
context.text: See, Renee? Somebody who knows spices.

context.speaker: renee
context.text: Fine, I'll allow it. What's your secret ingredient then?

question.speaker: jasmine
question.text: Good question! Mostly my grandma's recipe, but I always add a little cinnamon.

question.speaker: renee
question.text: Which I still think is weird.

humor.speaker: jasmine
humor.text: Told you this aisle has the best people.

intro.speaker: jasmine
intro.text: Nice to meet you! I'm Jasmine, and this is Renee.

intro.speaker: renee
intro.text: Hi. She introduces me before I can, every time.

inclusive.speaker: renee
inclusive.text: Look at that, somebody included me. I'm warming up to you.

pushy.speaker: renee
pushy.text: Okay, that's a little much. We're just shopping.

pushy.speaker: jasmine
pushy.text: Yeah... we should probably get going.

exit.speaker: renee
exit.text: Good luck with the cumin. Bye!

timeout.speaker: jasmine
timeout.text: Well, we've got to finish shopping. It was fun chatting!

rubric.label: Friendly opener
rubric.tip: Open with a simple, relaxed greeting.

rubric.label: Used the situation (the spices, the recipe)
rubric.tip: Mention something you both share right now, like the paprika. It feels natural, not like a line.

rubric.label: Asked open questions
rubric.tip: Ask an open question so they can talk too.

rubric.label: Included both people
rubric.tip: With two people, bring the friend in too. Ignoring her makes it awkward for both of them.

rubric.label: Light humor
rubric.tip: A little self-aware humor lowers the pressure.

rubric.label: Graceful exit
rubric.tip: End warmly while the energy is good. A polite exit is confident.

penalties.label: Pushy or appearance-focused remark
penalties.tip: Skip pushy or physical comments. Respect and comfort come first, and you'll be more attractive for it.
